title: Replace the 12 V battery
summary: Disconnect, swap and reconnect the starter battery in the right order.
interval: Typically four to six years. Slow cranking on a cold morning is the usual first symptom.
safety: A car battery can deliver hundreds of amps into a dropped spanner. Remove watches and rings, and never let a tool bridge both terminals.
Batteries vent hydrogen. No smoking, no sparks, no flames nearby.
The electrolyte is sulphuric acid. If the case is cracked or bulging, wear eye protection and gloves.

tools.name: Spanner or socket set (usually 10 mm and 13 mm)
Memory saver
tools.note: Keeps radio codes, window calibration and stored settings alive while the battery is out.

steps.title: Note anything the car will forget
steps.detail: Radio code, seat and mirror presets, clock. Some cars need the electric windows re-calibrated afterwards (hold the switch up for a few seconds at the top of travel).

steps.title: Everything off
steps.detail: Ignition off, key out, doors closed, bonnet light disconnected if it is the type that stays on. Wait a minute for modules to go to sleep.

steps.title: Find the battery
steps.detail: Usually under the bonnet, but plenty of cars put it in the boot, under the floor or under a front seat.

steps.title: Disconnect the negative terminal FIRST
steps.detail: Marked with a minus and usually a black cover. Slacken the clamp, twist it off and tuck it aside where it cannot spring back.
steps.warning: Negative first, always. If you start on the positive and your spanner touches bodywork, you short the battery through the tool.

steps.title: Disconnect the positive terminal
steps.detail: Slacken, remove, and put the insulating cover back over the terminal so nothing can touch it.

steps.title: Undo the hold-down clamp and lift the battery out
steps.detail: A long bolt at the base or a bar across the top. Batteries are heavier than they look — lift with your legs and keep it level.

steps.title: Clean the tray and terminals
steps.detail: Wire-brush any white or green corrosion off the clamps. Clean, bright metal makes the difference between a good connection and a mysterious no-start.

steps.title: Fit the new battery and secure it
steps.detail: Same orientation — check the terminals reach their cables before you tighten anything. Refit the hold-down clamp; an unsecured battery is an MOT failure.
steps.warning: A loose battery can tip, short against the bonnet, or crack its case.

steps.title: Reconnect positive FIRST, then negative
steps.detail: Exactly the reverse of removal. Tighten enough that the clamp cannot be twisted by hand, no more — the lead posts are soft.

steps.title: Start up and check
steps.detail: It should crank strongly. With the engine running, charging voltage at the terminals should sit around 13.5–14.8 V. Re-enter the radio code and reset the clock.

steps.title: Recycle the old battery
steps.detail: Any recycling centre or motor factor will take it, and many pay a small scrap value. Never put it in a household bin.
